chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the words of Lut (peace be upon him): 'These are my daughters, they are purer for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He presented to them for marriage.'
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Lut mean when he said 'These are my daughters' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the nature of Prophet Lut’s (peace be upon him) offer of his 'daughters' in Surah Hud, interpreting it as a proposal of marriage rather than sexual availability. This exegetical view, supported by scholars like Al-Tabari and Al-Qurtubi, suggests the 'daughters' were either his female guests or his actual kin, highlighting the cultural context of hospitality and kinship in pre-Islamic Arabia. The narration underscores the Imam’s role in resolving ambiguities in Quranic narratives through precise linguistic and contextual analysis.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the words of Lutas [11:78] These are my daughters (nation’s daughters)- they are purer for you. Heasws said: ‘Heas presented to them for the marriage’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Ya’qub bin Shu’ayb who has said the following: “About the words of Lot, ‘These are my daughters and they are cleaner and pure,’ [11:78] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He offered them for marriage.’”
